title: Lack of Association Between Heart Failure and Incident Cancer.
claim_supported: In 28,341 Physicians' Health Study participants with adjudicated outcomes and median 19.9-year follow-up, HF modelled as a time-varying exposure was NOT associated with cancer incidence (adjusted HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.86-1.29) or with cancer-specific mortality.

title: Recurrence of breast cancer after regional or general anaesthesia: a randomised controlled trial.
claim_supported: In a randomised trial of 2,108 women undergoing breast cancer resection, regional anaesthesia-analgesia (avoiding opioids and volatile agent) did not reduce recurrence versus general anaesthesia with opioid analgesia; the trial stopped for futility.

title: Epidural Anesthesia-Analgesia and Recurrence-free Survival after Lung Cancer Surgery: A Randomized Trial.
claim_supported: In 400 patients randomised during lung cancer surgery, epidural anaesthesia-analgesia did not improve recurrence-free survival (adjusted HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.60-1.35) versus general anaesthesia with intravenous opioids.

title: Association of Spironolactone Use With Risk of Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis.
claim_supported: Systematic review and meta-analysis of spironolactone, a drug given to most HF patients, and cancer risk - illustrating that HF pharmacotherapy is a candidate confounder for any HF-cancer association.

title: Tumor Growth Ameliorates Cardiac Dysfunction.
claim_supported: In the reciprocal direction, tumour-bearing mice subjected to pressure overload showed reduced cardiac hypertrophy, less fibrosis and improved contractile function, mediated by tumour-driven M1-to-M2 cardiac macrophage polarisation.

title: Tumor Progression Reverses Cardiac Hypertrophy and Fibrosis in a Tetracycline-Regulated ATF3 Transgenic Mouse Model.
claim_supported: Tumour progression reversed cardiac hypertrophy and fibrosis in a tetracycline-regulated ATF3 transgenic mouse model, further complicating a simple unidirectional HF-to-cancer narrative.

title: Comorbidity trajectories before and after the diagnosis of heart failure: A UK Biobank cohort study.
claim_supported: In UK Biobank, comorbidities accumulated for over a decade before HF diagnosis and cancer was among the diseases commonly immediately preceding HF, so HF is typically a late event in a multimorbidity trajectory rather than a clean baseline exposure.

title: Framingham risk score associates with incident cancer and heart failure.
claim_supported: The Framingham risk score, built from shared risk factors, predicted both incident cancer (sHR 2.32) and incident HF (sHR 10.08) in PREVEND with replication in UK Biobank, showing a shared risk-factor substrate can generate the HF-cancer association without HF causing cancer.

title: Patients with heart failure have an increased risk of incident cancer.
claim_supported: In the Olmsted County community cohort, HF patients had a 68% higher adjusted risk of incident cancer (HR 1.68, 95% CI 1.13-2.50) after adjustment for BMI, smoking and comorbidities; pre-index cancer history did not differ between cases and controls.

title: Incidence of cancer in patients with chronic heart failure: a long-term follow-up study.
claim_supported: In 9,307 Danish chronic HF outpatients the cancer incidence rate ratio versus the general population was 1.24 (95% CI 1.15-1.33), elevated in all age strata and for all major cancer types except prostate, and persisting beyond the first year after HF diagnosis.

title: Common risk factors for heart failure and cancer.
claim_supported: Review arguing that behavioural risk factors historically classified as cardiovascular equally predict cancer, so a holistic risk estimate is needed.

title: Does heart failure increase the risk of incident cancer? A meta-analysis and systematic review.
claim_supported: Meta-analysis of 4 cohort studies (5,004,251 participants) gave a pooled RR for incident cancer in HF of 1.22 (95% CI 1.13-1.33) and a pooled co-mortality RR of 2.03 (95% CI 1.13-3.65).

title: Differential risk of incident cancer in patients with heart failure: A nationwide population-based cohort study.
claim_supported: In 128,441 Korean HF patients the crude cancer HR was 1.64 (95% CI 1.61-1.68), but a 2-year lag analysis excluding early diagnoses attenuated this to HR 1.09 (95% CI 1.05-1.13), with only lung, hepatobiliary/pancreatic and haematologic cancers remaining consistently elevated.

title: Heart failure is associated with an increased incidence of cancer diagnoses.
claim_supported: In 100,124 matched German outpatient pairs, 25.7% of HF versus 16.2% of non-HF patients received a cancer diagnosis over 10 years (HR 1.76, 95% CI 1.71-1.81); matching included yearly consultation frequency.

title: Cancer Incidence and Mortality According to Pre-Existing Heart Failure in a Community-Based Cohort.
claim_supported: In 104,020 matched pairs from Puglia, cancer incidence was higher with pre-existing HF (HR 1.76) and cancer mortality far higher (HR 4.11; competing-risk subdistribution HR 3.48); among HF patients, high-dose loop diuretic prescription was itself associated with higher cancer incidence and mortality.

title: Association of inflammatory markers with incident heart failure or cancer in the HUNT3 and Health ABC population studies.
claim_supported: Baseline hsCRP was associated with incident HF or cancer in HUNT3 (HR 1.09) and Health ABC (HR 1.11), as were IL-1, IL-6 and TNF-alpha, supporting low-grade inflammation as a shared antecedent of both diseases.

title: Cancer and Cardiovascular Disease: Shared Risk Factors, Mechanisms, and Clinical Implications: JACC: CardioOncology State-of-the-Art Review.
claim_supported: JACC CardioOncology state-of-the-art review on shared risk factors and mechanisms (ageing, inflammation, metabolic dysregulation, clonal haematopoiesis) linking cancer and cardiovascular disease.

title: Global gene expression profiling in the failing myocardium.
claim_supported: Meta-analysis of failing-myocardium microarray datasets identified 107 recurrent HF-related genes including the extracellular molecules periostin, pleiotrophin and SERPINA3.

journal: Proc Natl Acad Sci U S A
title: Exogenously administered secreted frizzled related protein 2 (Sfrp2) reduces fibrosis and improves cardiac function in a rat model of myocardial infarction.
claim_supported: Endogenous Sfrp2 protein was upregulated in rat heart after myocardial infarction, and exogenous Sfrp2 reduced fibrosis and improved cardiac function by inhibiting Bmp1-mediated procollagen processing.

title: Follistatin-like 1 in chronic systolic heart failure: a marker of left ventricular remodeling.
claim_supported: Serum FSTL1 was 56% higher in chronic systolic HF patients than matched controls and predicted LV mass index, and FSTL1 protein was 2.5-fold higher in explanted failing than non-failing human hearts.

title: Thrombospondin-4 regulates fibrosis and remodeling of the myocardium in response to pressure overload.
claim_supported: TSP-4 (THBS4) expression increases markedly in hypertrophic and failing hearts in rodent models and in humans, and Thbs4-knockout mice showed greater cardiac fibrosis and worse functional parameters after transverse aortic constriction.

title: Deficiency of cartilage oligomeric matrix protein causes dilated cardiomyopathy.
claim_supported: COMP-knockout mice spontaneously developed dilated cardiomyopathy via reduced integrin beta-1 signalling, and COMP expression was DECREASED in DCM patient hearts versus donor hearts - the opposite direction to a HF-upregulated secreted ligand.

title: Periostin expression is upregulated and associated with myocardial fibrosis in human failing hearts.
claim_supported: Periostin mRNA was significantly increased in explanted human failing myocardium versus donor controls, was undetectable at protein level in controls, and its protein level correlated with myocardial fibrosis and LV diastolic dimension.

title: Connective tissue growth factor and cardiac diastolic dysfunction: human data from the Taiwan diastolic heart failure registry and molecular basis by cellular and animal models.
claim_supported: Plasma CTGF correlated with diastolic dysfunction severity (E/e') and MRI-assessed myocardial fibrosis in 125 diastolic HF patients, with stretch increasing CTGF secretion from cardiomyocytes in vitro and tissue CTGF rising in a canine aortic-banding model.

title: The inflammatory response in myocardial injury, repair, and remodelling.
claim_supported: Review establishing that myocardial injury triggers cytokine and chemokine upregulation in the infarcted and remodelling myocardium as part of the inflammatory response driving heart failure.

title: Endomyocardial expression of SDF-1 predicts mortality in patients with suspected myocarditis.
claim_supported: Endomyocardial CXCL12 (SDF-1) staining was positive in 65.4% of biopsies from inflammatory cardiomyopathy versus 19.1% of non-inflammatory cardiomyopathy, correlated with myocardial fibrosis, and predicted mortality in 174 non-ischaemic HF patients.

title: Follistatin like 1 Regulates Hypertrophy in Heart Failure with Preserved Ejection Fraction.
claim_supported: Blood FSTL1 was increased in humans with HFpEF and in hypertensive HFpEF mice, but cardiomyocyte-specific Fstl1 deletion worsened hypertrophy and diastolic dysfunction, so cardiac FSTL1 is protective rather than pathogenic.

title: Growth Differentiation Factor 15 as a Biomarker in Cardiovascular Disease.
claim_supported: GDF-15 is secreted in response to inflammation, oxidative stress and hypoxia; higher concentrations in community-dwelling individuals predict incident CVD, chronic kidney disease AND cancer independently of other biomarkers, and GDF-15 is independently associated with outcomes in HFpEF and HFrEF.

title: Meta-Analysis of the Usefulness of Plasma Galectin-3 to Predict the Risk of Mortality in Patients With Heart Failure and in the General Population.
claim_supported: Meta-analysis of 18 studies (32,350 participants) found each 1 SD increase in plasma galectin-3 associated with all-cause mortality (HR 1.10), CVD mortality (HR 1.22) and incident HF (HR 1.12).

title: Proenkephalin, Renal Dysfunction, and Prognosis in Patients With Acute Heart Failure: A GREAT Network Study.
claim_supported: In 1,908 acute HF patients, plasma proenkephalin A independently predicted 1-year mortality and worsening renal function; PENK is a stable surrogate for labile enkephalins and its main determinant was renal function, not cardiac status.

title: Plasma and Cardiac Galectin-3 in Patients With Heart Failure Reflects Both Inflammation and Fibrosis: Implications for Its Use as a Biomarker.
claim_supported: In endomyocardial biopsies, myocardial galectin-3 correlated with fibrosis in dilated cardiomyopathy and with inflammatory cell count in inflammatory cardiomyopathy, but plasma galectin-3 did NOT correlate with myocardial galectin-3 or LV fibrosis - a direct caveat on inferring cardiac secretion from plasma levels.

title: CTGF/CCN2 is an autocrine regulator of cardiac fibrosis.
claim_supported: Cell-specific deletion showed CCN2 from activated fibroblasts, not from cardiomyocytes (its main cardiac source), drives cardiac fibrosis and that CCN2 acts in an autocrine fashion - a direct caveat against treating cardiac CCN2 as an endocrine tumour-promoting signal.

title: Cardiometabolic Biomarkers and Their Temporal Patterns Predict Poor Outcome in Chronic Heart Failure (Bio-SHiFT Study).
claim_supported: Serially measured IGFBP-7 levels and their slopes independently predicted the composite endpoint in 263 chronic HF patients after adjustment for NT-proBNP and troponin.

title: Natriuretic peptides in human heart: Novel insight into their molecular forms, functions, and diagnostic use.
claim_supported: ANP and BNP plasma concentrations and expression are elevated with volume and wall-stress load in human heart failure, but the circulating molecular forms are heterogeneous, with weakly active proBNP predominating.

title: Proenkephalin, an Opioid System Surrogate, as a Novel Comprehensive Renal Marker in Heart Failure.
claim_supported: In 2,180 BIOSTAT-CHF patients with validation in 1,703 more, PENK was elevated above the 99th percentile in 57%, but its strongest independent predictor was eGFR and it clustered with renal markers, so elevated PENK in HF primarily reflects kidney function.

title: Role of Sfrps in cardiovascular disease.
claim_supported: Review of secreted frizzled-related proteins in cardiovascular disease, reporting involvement in myocardial infarction, cardiac remodelling and heart failure while stating that the overall role of Sfrps in cardiac disease is unknown.

title: Cardiac natriuretic peptides.
claim_supported: Authoritative review establishing ANP (NPPA) and BNP (NPPB) as cardiomyocyte-secreted hormones signalling through membrane guanylyl cyclase receptors, with plasma levels serving as diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers of heart disease.

title: Pathophysiological pathways related to high plasma growth differentiation factor 15 concentrations in patients with heart failure.
claim_supported: In 2,279 HF patients with validation in 1,705, high plasma GDF-15 marked activation of inflammatory pathways including IL-6 response, TNF/death receptor activity and T-cell differentiation, and predicted mortality and HF hospitalisation.

title: Targeting immune-fibroblast cell communication in heart failure.
claim_supported: Multiomic single-cell profiling of 45 healthy, infarcted and chronically failing human hearts identified a FAP/POSTN-expressing matrifibrocyte population arising via macrophage IL-1beta signalling, localising periostin production to a disease-associated human cardiac fibroblast state.

title: IGFBP7 and Heart Failure: From Senescence Biomarker to Therapeutic Target.
claim_supported: Review concluding circulating IGFBP7 is strongly associated with HF development and progression, with cell-specific actions: cardiomyocyte-derived IGFBP7 signals through IGF-1R while endothelial-derived IGFBP7 inhibits cardiomyocyte insulin receptor signalling.

title: The Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia enables predictive modelling of anticancer drug sensitivity.
claim_supported: The Cancer Cell Line Encyclopedia: gene expression, copy number and sequencing across 947 human cancer cell lines with pharmacological profiles, enabling lineage-level expression comparisons.

title: The Cancer Genome Atlas Pan-Cancer analysis project.
claim_supported: The TCGA Pan-Cancer analysis project, providing matched multi-platform molecular profiles across tumour types for cross-lineage comparison.

title: Proteomics. Tissue-based map of the human proteome.
claim_supported: Tissue-based map of the human proteome integrating quantitative tissue transcriptomics with immunohistochemistry across 32 tissues, used to define the human secretome and cancer proteome.

first_author: [consortium authorship; no individual author in PubMed record]
title: Human genomics. The Genotype-Tissue Expression (GTEx) pilot analysis: multitissue gene regulation in humans.
claim_supported: GTEx pilot analysis of RNA sequencing from 1,641 samples across 43 tissues in 175 individuals, establishing the reference for normal human tissue expression.

title: CellPhoneDB: inferring cell-cell communication from combined expression of multi-subunit ligand-receptor complexes.
claim_supported: CellPhoneDB provides a ligand-receptor repository that accounts for multi-subunit complex architecture plus a statistical framework for inferring enriched cell-type interactions from single-cell transcriptomics.

title: Inference and analysis of cell-cell communication using CellChat.
claim_supported: CellChat infers intercellular communication from single-cell RNA-seq using a curated ligand-receptor-cofactor database, the canonical approach to expression-based ligand-receptor inference.

title: Identifying plasma proteomic signatures from health to heart failure, across the ejection fraction spectrum.
claim_supported: Comparison of 4,210 circulating proteins across 739 patients spanning healthy, Stage A/B, HFpEF and ischaemic HFrEF found 2,122 proteins differentially expressed in iHFrEF but only 52 in HFpEF versus healthy, showing the HF plasma proteome is strongly phenotype-dependent.

title: Integrative proteomic analyses across common cardiac diseases yield mechanistic insights and enhanced prediction.
claim_supported: Analysis of 1,459 proteins in 44,313 UK Biobank participants identified 820 protein-disease associations across coronary artery disease, HF, atrial fibrillation and aortic stenosis, but cis-Mendelian randomisation supported causal roles for only about 4% of proteins.

title: Advances and challenges in cell-cell communication inference: a comprehensive review of tools, resources, and future directions.
claim_supported: Review of over 100 cell-cell communication inference tools and nearly 50 ligand-receptor resources, cataloguing their differing assumptions and limitations and the unresolved pitfalls of expression-based interaction inference.

title: The biology of the opioid growth factor receptor (OGFr).
claim_supported: The OGF receptor is a nuclear-envelope-associated protein with no structural homology to the classical opioid receptors, so enkephalin growth effects need not run through OPRK1/OPRD1/OPRM1.

title: Connective tissue growth factor and its role in lung adenocarcinoma invasion and metastasis.
claim_supported: CTGF overexpression REDUCED invasive and metastatic activity of lung adenocarcinoma cells via integrin alpha-v beta-3/beta-5-dependent CRMP-1 induction, showing CCN2-integrin signalling can be anti-metastatic depending on tumour type.

title: Atrial natriuretic peptides: anticancer agents.
claim_supported: ANP-family peptides at micromolar concentrations reduced pancreatic, breast and lung cancer cell numbers in culture, whereas BNP had no effect even at 100-fold higher concentration - i.e. reported anticancer activity is peptide-specific and at supraphysiological doses.

title: Frequent epigenetic inactivation of Wnt antagonist genes in breast cancer.
claim_supported: SFRP1, SFRP2 and SFRP5 were methylated in most breast cancer cell lines and primary tumours, and SFRP overexpression inhibited cancer cell growth - so more SFRP ligand would be predicted to restrain, not promote, Wnt-driven tumours.

title: The opioid growth factor (OGF) and low dose naltrexone (LDN) suppress human ovarian cancer progression in mice.
claim_supported: Opioid growth factor (met-enkephalin) and low-dose naltrexone each reduced SKOV-3 ovarian tumour burden in nude mice by inhibiting proliferation and angiogenesis, implicating the OGF-OGFr axis rather than the classical GPCR opioid receptors.

title: κ-Opioid receptor in the nucleus is a novel prognostic factor of esophageal squamous cell carcinoma.
claim_supported: KOR protein was upregulated in oesophageal squamous cell carcinoma versus non-tumour epithelium, and high nuclear KOR expression was an independent predictor of poorer prognosis in 256 cases.

title: Thrombospondin-4 expression is activated during the stromal response to invasive breast cancer.
claim_supported: THBS4 was absent from normal breast epithelium and matrix but significantly induced in cancer-associated stroma versus normal stroma and epithelium, with rare genomic alteration - i.e. a stromal, microenvironment-induced response rather than a tumour-cell-autonomous receptor axis.

title: Opioid requirement, opioid receptor expression, and clinical outcomes in patients with advanced prostate cancer.
claim_supported: In metastatic prostate cancer, higher tumour MOR expression and greater opioid requirement were independently associated with shorter progression-free and overall survival, with validation in a national registry cohort.

title: к Opioids inhibit tumor angiogenesis by suppressing VEGF signaling.
claim_supported: Kappa opioid receptor agonists inhibited endothelial migration and tube formation by suppressing VEGFR2, and tumours in KOR-knockout mice grew faster with enhanced angiogenesis - i.e. KOR signalling was anti-tumorigenic here.

title: Secreted frizzled related proteins: Implications in cancers.
claim_supported: Review establishing SFRPs as extracellular Wnt inhibitors that bind Wnt ligands or Frizzled receptors, whose genes are frequently silenced by promoter hypermethylation across cancers, consistent with a tumour-suppressor role.

title: Increased μ-opioid receptor expression in metastatic lung cancer.
claim_supported: MOR immunostaining was significantly higher in lung cancer than adjacent normal lung and roughly two-fold higher in metastatic cases.

title: The non-canonical Wnt ligand, Wnt5a, is upregulated and associated with epithelial to mesenchymal transition in epithelial ovarian cancer.
claim_supported: In 623 patients, the non-canonical Wnt ligand WNT5A was upregulated across all major epithelial ovarian cancer subtypes versus borderline and benign tumours, and recombinant WNT5A reduced adhesion and induced EMT in ovarian surface epithelial cells.

title: A noncanonical Frizzled2 pathway regulates epithelial-mesenchymal transition and metastasis.
claim_supported: FZD2 and its ligands WNT5A/WNT5B were elevated in metastatic cancer cell lines and high-grade tumours, and FZD2 drove EMT and migration through a noncanonical Fyn-STAT3 pathway; an anti-FZD2 antibody inhibited tumour growth and metastasis in xenografts.

title: Low levels of IGFBP7 expression in high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma is associated with patient outcome.
claim_supported: In high-grade serous ovarian carcinoma IGFBP7 expression was significantly LOWER than in normal ovarian surface epithelium, with LOH and promoter methylation, so the direction of IGFBP7 effect is tumour-type dependent.

title: Relationship between expression of IGFBP7 and clinicopathological variables in gastric cancer.
claim_supported: In 219 gastric cancer patients IGFBP7 protein overexpression correlated with invasion depth, nodal and distant metastasis and worse disease-specific survival (HR 4.8).

title: Natriuretic peptide receptor A inhibition suppresses gastric cancer development through reactive oxygen species-mediated G2/M cell cycle arrest and cell death.
claim_supported: NPR1 (NPRA) expression correlated positively with gastric tumour size and stage, and NPR1 knockdown induced ROS-mediated G2/M arrest and cell death, so NPR1 signalling was pro-tumorigenic in this model.

title: Non-homeostatic body weight regulation through a brainstem-restricted receptor for GDF15.
claim_supported: GFRAL, the receptor for GDF15, is restricted to the area postrema and nucleus tractus solitarius of the brainstem, so circulating GDF15 acting through its canonical receptor cannot signal directly to peripheral tumour cells.

title: Blocking the FSTL1-DIP2A Axis Improves Anti-tumor Immunity.
claim_supported: DIP2A is the receptor for FSTL1 and its expression in tumour cells is critical for FSTL1-induced immunoresistance; FSTL1/DIP2A co-positivity correlated with poor prognosis in NSCLC.

title: Frizzled 2-induced epithelial-mesenchymal transition correlates with vasculogenic mimicry, stemness, and Hippo signaling in hepatocellular carcinoma.
claim_supported: FZD2 was highly expressed in two cohorts of hepatitis B-related hepatocellular carcinoma, high expression associated with poor prognosis, and FZD2 drove EMT, stem-like properties and vasculogenic mimicry.

title: Host Wnt5a Potentiates Microenvironmental Regulation of Ovarian Cancer Metastasis.
claim_supported: Host-derived WNT5A secreted by peritoneal mesothelial cells and visceral adipose promoted ovarian cancer peritoneal metastasis, and conditional host Wnt5a knockout significantly reduced metastatic burden - establishing a host-secreted ligand axis in gynaecologic cancer.

title: Opioid receptors beyond pain control: The role in cancer pathology and the debated importance of their pharmacological modulation.
claim_supported: Review concluding that evidence for opioid receptor agonists in human cancer is conflicting, with both cancer-promoting and cancer-suppressing findings reported and tissue receptor expression varying by tumour type.

title: Antibody-mediated inhibition of GDF15-GFRAL activity reverses cancer cachexia in mice.
claim_supported: An antagonistic anti-GFRAL antibody reversed cancer cachexia in tumour-bearing mice via a peripheral sympathetic lipolytic axis, so the established GDF15 role in cancer is host wasting rather than direct tumour growth promotion.

title: Periostincancer-associated fibroblasts promote lymph node metastasis by impairing the lymphatic endothelial barriers in cervical squamous cell carcinoma.
claim_supported: A periostin-high cancer-associated fibroblast subset in cervical squamous cell carcinoma correlated with lymph node metastasis and poor survival and impaired lymphatic endothelial barriers via integrin-FAK/Src-VE-cadherin signalling.

title: Thrombospondin 4/integrin α2/HSF1 axis promotes proliferation and cancer stem-like traits of gallbladder cancer by enhancing reciprocal crosstalk between cancer-associated fibroblasts and tumor cells.
claim_supported: CAF-derived TSP-4 bound integrin alpha-2 on gallbladder cancer cells to phosphorylate HSF1 and promote proliferation, EMT and stem-like traits, giving THBS4 a defined receptor in cancer.

title: Overexpression of SERPINA3 promotes tumor invasion and migration, epithelial-mesenchymal-transition in triple-negative breast cancer cells.
claim_supported: SERPINA3 was upregulated in breast cancer tissue and its overexpression promoted proliferation, migration, invasion and EMT in triple-negative cell lines - i.e. tumour-promoting in breast cancer, opposite to the lung finding.

title: Wnt5A modulates integrin expression in a receptor-dependent manner in ovarian cancer cells.
claim_supported: WNT5A overexpression in ovarian cancer cells upregulated FZD2 and FZD5, increased alpha-v integrin expression, proliferation and migration, and a FZD5 antagonist abrogated these effects, connecting non-canonical Wnt-Frizzled signalling to integrin biology in ovarian cancer.

title: FZD2 promotes TGF-β-induced epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition in breast cancer via activating notch signaling pathway.
claim_supported: FZD2 mRNA and protein were abundant in breast cancer tissue, high FZD2 correlated with poor prognosis, and FZD2 silencing suppressed growth, migration, invasion and xenograft tumour growth via TGF-beta1-dependent EMT.

title: FSTL1 Secreted by Activated Fibroblasts Promotes Hepatocellular Carcinoma Metastasis and Stemness.
claim_supported: FSTL1 secreted by activated hepatic fibroblasts promoted hepatocellular carcinoma growth, metastasis and stemness by binding TLR4 and activating AKT/mTOR/4EBP1; FSTL1 blockade reduced malignancy in a preclinical model.

title: Solid Tumor Opioid Receptor Expression and Oncologic Outcomes: Analysis of the Cancer Genome Atlas and Genotype Tissue Expression Project.
claim_supported: Across 8,780 TCGA and GTEx samples from twelve solid tumour types, KOR (OPRK1, OR 1.27), DOR (OPRD1, OR 1.66) and OGFR (OR 2.39) were more expressed in tumour than normal tissue while MOR (OPRM1, OR 0.74) was less; after adjustment, tumour opioid receptor expression was NOT associated with disease-free interval or overall survival.

title: Unfolding the cascade of SERPINA3: Inflammation to cancer.
claim_supported: Review concluding SERPINA3 has cancer- and compartment-specific functions, acting as a tumour promoter in some cancers and a suppressor in others, with its mechanism and effectors still obscure.

title: STAT3 is Activated by CTGF-mediated Tumor-stroma Cross Talk to Promote HCC Progression.
claim_supported: Hepatoma-derived CTGF stimulated integrin/NF-kB signalling in stromal cells to upregulate IL-6 family cytokines that reactivated gp130/STAT3 in tumour cells; hepatocyte CTGF knockout suppressed tumour progression.

title: Cartilage oligomeric matrix protein acts as a molecular biomarker in multiple cancer types.
claim_supported: Pan-cancer analysis found COMP significantly overexpressed in 15 human cancers with diagnostic ROC performance across 16 tumour types and association with immune evasion.

title: Periostin promotes ovarian cancer metastasis by enhancing M2 macrophages and cancer-associated fibroblasts via integrin-mediated NF-κB and TGF-β2 signaling.
claim_supported: Periostin colocalised with integrin beta-3 and beta-5 in ovarian cancer cells and drove integrin/ERK/NF-kB signalling; POSTN overexpression increased migration, invasion and in vivo metastasis while knockdown reduced them.

title: Overexpression of SERPINA3 suppresses tumor progression by modulating SPOP/NF‑κB in lung cancer.
claim_supported: SERPINA3 was downregulated in lung cancer tissues and cell lines, and overexpression inhibited growth, migration and invasion and slowed xenograft growth - i.e. tumour-suppressive in lung cancer.

title: CXCL12-CXCR4/CXCR7 Axis in Cancer: from Mechanisms to Clinical Applications.
claim_supported: Review establishing the CXCL12-CXCR4/CXCR7 axis as a driver of tumour proliferation, survival, angiogenesis and metastasis across multiple cancers.

title: Therapeutic antibody targeting natriuretic peptide receptor 1 inhibits gastric cancer growth via BCL-2-mediated intrinsic apoptosis.
claim_supported: NPR1 mRNA was upregulated in gastric cancer cell lines, silencing attenuated proliferation, invasion and migration, and an anti-NPR1 antibody reduced peritoneal tumour burden in xenografted mice; high tumour NPR1 predicted recurrence and poorer prognosis.

title: Pan-cancer profiling of FZD2 as a prognostic biomarker: integrative multi-omics analysis with experimental validation and functional characterization in gastric cancer.
claim_supported: Pan-cancer multi-omics profiling found FZD2 significantly upregulated in several malignancies including stomach, bladder and cholangiocarcinoma, with siRNA knockdown reducing gastric cancer proliferation and xenograft growth.

title: Clonal hematopoiesis associated with TET2 deficiency accelerates atherosclerosis development in mice.
claim_supported: TET2-deficient clonal haematopoiesis markedly increased atherosclerotic plaque size in Ldlr-null mice with increased NLRP3-mediated IL-1beta secretion, giving a causal mechanism for the CHIP-CVD link.

title: Clonal Hematopoiesis and Risk of Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease.
claim_supported: CHIP carriers had 1.9-fold higher coronary heart disease risk and 4.0-fold higher early-onset MI risk; Tet2 perturbation in atherosclerosis-prone mice supported causality, establishing a somatic-mutation substrate shared by haematologic cancer and CVD.

title: Effect of interleukin-1β inhibition with canakinumab on incident lung cancer in patients with atherosclerosis: exploratory results from a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial.
claim_supported: In CANTOS, IL-1beta inhibition with canakinumab reduced incident lung cancer in patients with atherosclerosis and elevated hsCRP, providing randomised human evidence that an inflammatory pathway shared with CVD is causal for cancer incidence.

title: Heart Failure Stimulates Tumor Growth by Circulating Factors.
claim_supported: Myocardial infarction-induced HF increased intestinal tumour load 2.4-fold in APC-mutant mice, including in a heterotopic transplant model that excludes haemodynamic impairment; candidate secreted mediators included serpinA3, serpinA1, fibronectin and ceruloplasmin.

title: Response by Meijers and de Boer to Letters Regarding Article, "Heart Failure Stimulates Tumor Growth by Circulating Factors".
claim_supported: PubMed records two Letters (Comment type) on the 2018 Meijers HF-tumour paper plus this published Response by the original authors, documenting that the causal interpretation was contested in print; the letters carry no abstract so their specific arguments are not verifiable from the bibliographic record.

title: Clonal haematopoiesis: connecting ageing and inflammation in cardiovascular disease.
claim_supported: Review positioning CHIP as a common condition connecting ageing, inflammation, haematological cancer and a doubling of atherosclerotic CVD risk.

title: Reverse Cardio-Oncology: Cancer Development in Patients With Cardiovascular Disease.
claim_supported: Names and defines 'reverse cardio-oncology' as cancer development in patients with cardiovascular disease.

title: Early Cardiac Remodeling Promotes Tumor Growth and Metastasis.
claim_supported: Pressure-overload cardiac remodelling by transverse aortic constriction, without overt heart failure, produced larger primary tumours and more metastases; serum from TAC mice promoted cancer cell proliferation, and periostin depletion from that serum abolished the effect.

title: Myocardial infarction accelerates breast cancer via innate immune reprogramming.
claim_supported: Myocardial infarction accelerated breast tumour outgrowth in mice via epigenetic reprogramming of Ly6C-high bone marrow monocytes to an immunosuppressive phenotype; monocyte depletion abrogated the effect, and early-stage breast cancer patients with post-diagnosis cardiovascular events had higher recurrence and cancer-specific death.

title: Common mechanistic pathways in cancer and heart failure. A scientific roadmap on behalf of the Translational Research Committee of the Heart Failure Association (HFA) of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC).
claim_supported: HFA/ESC scientific roadmap on common mechanistic pathways in cancer and HF, identifying inflammation, metabolic reprogramming, clonal haematopoiesis, angiogenesis and stroma as shared, and calling for models where both pathologies coexist.

title: Development of Cancer in Patients With Heart Failure: How Systemic Inflammation Can Lay the Groundwork.
claim_supported: Review proposing chronic low-grade systemic inflammation and cardiokine secretion as the pathophysiological link from failing heart to carcinogenesis, while critically discussing the limitations of the supporting studies.

title: Clonal Hematopoiesis and Risk of Progression of Heart Failure With Reduced Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction.
claim_supported: In 62 HF patients with LVEF<45%, DNMT3A or TET2 CHIP mutations were associated with accelerated HF progression (death HR 2.79; death or HF hospitalisation HR 3.84) irrespective of ischaemic aetiology.

title: TET2-Driven Clonal Hematopoiesis and Response to Canakinumab: An Exploratory Analysis of the CANTOS Randomized Clinical Trial.
claim_supported: Exploratory CANTOS analysis of TET2-driven clonal haematopoiesis and cardiovascular response to canakinumab, in which TET2 variants were more common than DNMT3A in this hsCRP-selected population.

title: Clonal hematopoiesis, somatic mosaicism, and age-associated disease.
claim_supported: Physiological Reviews synthesis of clonal haematopoiesis and age-associated disease, noting most CHIP carriers never develop blood cancer while CHIP still associates with all-cause mortality and cardiovascular disease.

title: CHIP Happens: Clonal Hematopoiesis of Indeterminate Potential and Its Relationship to Solid Tumors.
claim_supported: Review reporting high rates of CHIP in patients with solid tumours, driven partly by oncologic therapy, and associations between CHIP and differential solid-tumour outcomes.

title: Clonal Hematopoiesis in Clinical and Experimental Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction.
claim_supported: TET2-mediated clonal haematopoiesis was enriched in HFpEF patients versus controls (12% vs 0%) and associated with worse diastolic dysfunction, with causality tested in a murine model.

title: Heart Failure Promotes Cancer Progression in an Integrin β1-Dependent Manner.
claim_supported: In Postn-knockout mice, cardiac-remodelling-dependent tumour promotion persisted, whereas integrin beta-1 loss-of-function in cancer cells abolished it, indicating the effect is mediated by multiple integrin-binding ligands rather than periostin alone.

title: Heart Failure Post-Myocardial Infarction Promotes Mammary Tumor Growth Through the NGF-TRKA Pathway.
claim_supported: Post-MI heart failure promoted 4T1 mammary tumour growth in BALB/c mice through elevated circulating NGF acting on TRKA-PI3K-AKT; TRKA inhibition suppressed tumour volume in MI mice.

title: Small Extracellular Vesicles From Infarcted and Failing Heart Accelerate Tumor Growth.
claim_supported: Small extracellular vesicles from post-MI hearts and cardiac mesenchymal stromal cells carried protumorigenic cargo and accelerated lung tumour growth on adoptive transfer; the effect differed by cancer type, being larger for lung and colon than for melanoma and breast lines.

title: Association of clonal haematopoiesis with heart failure incidence and outcomes: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
claim_supported: Meta-analysis of 57,755 participants found clonal haematopoiesis associated with incident HF (HR 1.23, 95% CI 1.12-1.35) and, in established HF, with all-cause mortality (HR 1.95).

title: Forward and reverse cardio-oncology.
claim_supported: Comprehensive Physiological Reviews treatment of forward and reverse cardio-oncology, describing HF-driven tumour promotion via a protumour cardiac secretome, immune modulation and the gut microbiome, and explicitly posing shared risk factors as the alternative explanation.
